technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring Cloud Stream and Spring XD repository conventions, extension points, and dependency-management approach rather than introducing a new runtime model.
Target Java 17 or newer and align implementation with Spring Framework 6-era APIs and configuration-property binding.
Implement U1 as an in-process test harness using embedded channels or test binders, avoiding external Redis, RabbitMQ, or other message-bus infrastructure.
Use Spring Boot configuration-property binding and application-context startup in tests so module wiring and configuration combinations are exercised together.
Provide fluent or idiomatic assertions through existing Spring test utilities and Hamcrest-compatible assertions where practical.
Treat the YARN work as an investigation and working prototype of the deployment SPI, with a documented strategy for a future YARNModuleDeployer rather than production-grade cluster operations.
Implement Redis Sentinel support through the existing Redis client and Spring integration abstractions, preserving a common message-bus contract for streams and batch pipelines.
Upgrade receptor-client behind its existing abstraction boundary, adapting request, response, and error handling to the latest Receptor API while preserving compatibility where feasible.
Implement singlenode binder auto-configuration using conditional bean creation, metadata for configuration properties, and dependency-based activation.
Pass YARN definition parameters through container launch configuration and expose them to the module using standard environment or application-argument mechanisms.
Use automated unit, integration, and regression tests as the primary acceptance mechanism, with external infrastructure limited to containerized or test-controlled services where required.
assumptions: The increment includes all eight user stories and development is performed by one software developer.
Existing repositories, build infrastructure, module APIs, and baseline implementations are available and buildable; no framework-wide redesign is required.

The exact versions of Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, Redis client, Receptor, Hadoop, and YARN are not specified, so compatible versions will be selected from the existing project dependency management.

U2 is limited to technical investigation, a demonstrable SPI prototype, and an implementation strategy; it does not include production hardening, security integration, performance qualification, or full cluster certification.
U3 assumes the trigger module already exists in Spring XD and can be migrated without redesigning its public behavior or adding new trigger types.
U4 assumes Redis Sentinel is used for high availability of the existing Redis-based message bus; Redis Cluster sharding, data migration, and operational tooling are out of scope.
U5 assumes the receptor-client has a localized integration surface and that the latest Receptor API documentation or compatible server behavior is available.
U6 is limited to making the existing Spring Cloud Data Flow administration UI client work with the required server configuration; creating a new UI is out of scope.
U7 is limited to singlenode binder auto-configuration, property metadata, and representative application-context tests; it does not include a new binder protocol.
U8 assumes definition parameters can be serialized through the existing YARN launch path and exposed as module arguments or environment properties without changes to the YARN runtime itself.
Documentation covers configuration, usage examples, limitations, and migration notes but not a complete end-user guide.
Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, local debugging, and release-oriented validation, but excludes elapsed waiting time and work by other teams.

activities.activity_description: Analyze the eight user stories, map them to existing modules and extension points, identify dependencies and compatibility constraints, and define acceptance scenarios and implementation boundaries.
Set up or verify the local build, inspect existing module, binder, deployer, receptor, and administration-client structures, and establish test and dependency-management conventions.

Implement the U1 test support for starting module application contexts, applying configuration properties, wiring module inputs and outputs, and sending and receiving data without an external message bus.

activities.activity_name: Test assertions, configuration coverage, and examples
activities.activity_description: Add idiomatic assertion support, representative property-combination tests, negative configuration tests, usage examples, and test-harness documentation for module authors.

Investigate the existing deployment abstractions and YARN APIs, identify required lifecycle and resource mappings, and implement a small working prototype demonstrating the proposed YARN deployment SPI.
Document the YARNModuleDeployer strategy, evaluate failure and lifecycle behavior, add focused tests or mocks for the SPI, and record unresolved production concerns.

Move the trigger module from the Spring XD area into the Spring Cloud Stream repository, adapt package and build metadata, preserve its source behavior, and integrate it with the existing module conventions.

Extend Redis message-bus configuration and connection handling to support Sentinel clusters, including master discovery, configurable sentinel properties, lifecycle behavior, and compatibility with stream and batch pipeline usage.
Create test coverage for Sentinel configuration, failover or reconnect behavior where practical, message production and consumption, and regression coverage for standalone Redis usage.
Update receptor-client dependencies and integration code for the latest Receptor API, adapt changed models and endpoints, preserve error handling, and update compatibility tests.

Configure and validate the existing administration UI client against the required Spring Cloud Data Flow server settings, including endpoint, authentication, proxy, and compatibility configuration as applicable.
Implement conditional auto-configuration for singlenode binder properties and beans, add configuration metadata, support dependency-based activation, and verify override behavior.
Extend YARN container launch data to carry definition parameters, map them into the launched module's arguments or environment, and add tests proving that parameters are available at runtime.

Run end-to-end and regression validation across migrated modules, binders, Redis modes, deployment paths, configuration auto-setup, receptor integration, and existing functionality; fix defects found during validation.
Document new test-harness usage, Redis Sentinel configuration, trigger-module availability, receptor-client changes, singlenode auto-configuration, YARN parameters, and known limitations.

activities.activity_name: Release preparation and final quality checks
activities.activity_description: Perform final clean builds, static checks, dependency and licensing verification, test-suite execution, packaging validation, change-log preparation, and release-candidate cleanup.
